text.p: Bankgesellschaft Berlin's management board chairman told a newspaper the bank would consider either buying another bank wholesale or picking out various portions in its quest to strengthen its position.

In an interview with German daily Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Wolfgang Rupf said Bankgesellschaft's existing weaknesses could not be removed solely through a stronger equity base or higher profits.
The main challenge, Rupf told the newspaper, was to create the capacities needed to build up investment banking, international project financing or private sector banking.

To achieve that, Rupf said "either we buy into an existing institution and there is not only BHF Bank." Or Rupf said the group could also consider buying only certain bits of a bank or certain employees.

Bankgesellschaft has been rumoured to be keenly interested in acquiring Frankfurt-based BHF Bank, but Rupf again said that Bankgesellschaft was not only interested in BHF Bank, stressing there were other groups Bankgesellschaft might be interested in. Bankgesellschaft recently announced plans to buy regional bank NordLB.
Rupf said the group would decide by the end of the year on whether it would buy another bank in its entirety or simply buy certain portions.
